name: luna-shopper-backend
//: Umbrella project for the Luna Shopper backend (plans 0013, 0015). It has no build; it hosts the cross-service test-data orchestrator targets (seed / db:snapshot / db:restore) and the stack targets that wrap compose + migrations + a suite in one command. The services themselves — luna-shopper-backend-auth, -core, -catalog, -gateway, -realtime — are their own nested projects under this directory. Pass args after `--`, e.g. `nx run luna-shopper-backend:db:snapshot -- --label initial`.

stack:bootstrap.//: Writes whatever a local stack needs and does not have: the six git ignored service .env files (from the slot 0 defaults) and the throwaway dev JWT keypair. Idempotent, and never overwrites a file that already exists. stack:up runs it first, so this is only needed to configure a checkout without starting anything.

stack:up.//: Plan 0015, section 4. Configures the checkout first (see stack:bootstrap), then brings the compose stack up honoring .env.slot, waits on every healthcheck (`up --wait`, never a sleep), and runs migration:run for auth, core and catalog.

stack:down.//: Tears the stack down INCLUDING volumes, so nothing survives between runs. This is the whole project, so it takes any profiled containers (observability, test) with it.

observability:up.//: Plan 0016, section 9. Starts ONLY the four containers of the opt-in `observability` compose profile: the OTLP collector, Jaeger, Prometheus and Grafana. It does not start the base stack and does not migrate, so run stack:up first (or alongside) for the databases. Prints the URLs it just published, on this slot's ports. The services already point at the collector (luna-slot.sh writes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT into each service .env), so nothing else has to change for spans to start landing.

observability:down.//: Removes ONLY the four observability containers and leaves the databases, NATS and Mailpit running. Unlike stack:down it also keeps the volumes, so the Prometheus history and any Grafana dashboard survive. Use stack:down to take everything down instead.

test-integration:stack.//: stack:up, then run-many -t test-integration with LUNA_INTEGRATION=1, then stack:down in a guaranteed cleanup step — the suite's exit code survives the teardown. This is the same sequence CI runs.

e2e:stack.//: stack:up, build and start the five services, gate on /health/ready, run the Playwright suite, then stop the services and tear the stack down whatever happened.
